profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a fintech company preparing a joint internal briefing for executives and external partners on a proposed algorithmic stablecoin design inspired by recent research on optimal algorithmic monetary policy. The product strategy workstream is assembling the briefing narrative and comparative-statistics takeaways, while the policy partnerships workstream is packaging the same material for conversations with a central bank innovation office and two regulated payment partners. The meeting is meant to align on handoffs for the 'policy memo,' the latest model outputs, ownership of the shared briefing deck, and what counts as a 'final' package for circulation by Thursday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on who updates which materials, which version of the model results will be reflected, and when the package is ready to send onward.

members.name: Ava Chen
members.expertise: Fintech product strategy, token mechanism positioning, executive communications
members.background: Former management consultant who moved into digital assets strategy; she translates quantitative research into business-facing narratives and coordinates cross-functional launch materials.
members.private_state: She wants to lock the executive story quickly so leadership can approve the pilot narrative this week, and she is trying to avoid reopening framing debates that would slow down deck production.
hidden_assumptions: The 'policy memo' is the 6-page executive-facing summary attached to the board-prep deck, not the longer technical annex used by external policy teams.
The 'latest run' means the calibrated results from last Friday's parameter sweep that her strategy team already used in slide drafts, unless someone explicitly flags a methodological change.
A deliverable is 'final' once the narrative, charts, and key messages are stable enough for leadership review, even if formatting and appendix footnotes are still cleaned up later.
Updating the shared deck includes preserving the current executive storyline and swapping in refreshed charts, not broadening the scope to include implementation or compliance caveats unless asked.

members.name: Marcus Alvarez
members.expertise: Regulatory engagement, public-sector stakeholder management, policy translation for digital payments
members.background: Former payments policy advisor at a national regulator; he now manages relationships with central bank and banking-sector counterparts and prepares materials suitable for external circulation.
members.private_state: He wants the package to be robust enough for outside stakeholders so he does not risk sending material that appears under-specified or commercially biased in front of policy counterparts.
hidden_assumptions: The 'policy memo' is the externally shareable 10-page note with methodological caveats and public-sector implications, because that is the document his partners expect under that label.
The 'latest run' means the most recent model output in the research folder, including the weekend rerun with tighter volatility assumptions and updated comparative-statics tables.
A package is only 'final' when it is suitable for external circulation: numbers frozen, caveats included, references checked, and the appendix aligned with the main deck.
Refreshing the shared deck naturally includes adding policy guardrails, implementation assumptions, and CBDC comparison slides because those are inseparable from partner-facing use of the material.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss 'the policy memo' as if it is a single agreed document.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Ava means the concise internal executive memo summarizing the stablecoin rule, trade-off intuition, and headline implications for product positioning.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the external-facing policy note that includes methodological caveats, comparative-statics interpretation, and CBDC/public-sector framing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations commonly use the phrase 'policy memo,' and in a coordination meeting it sounds like an established artifact rather than something requiring definition; each assumes the other is referring to the obvious memo used in their own workflow.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest run' is being handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use 'the latest run' for charts and talking points.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Ava is thinking of Friday's calibrated parameter sweep that underpins the draft executive deck already circulated internally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is thinking of the weekend rerun saved in the research folder that uses updated volatility bounds and produces slightly different supply-stability trade-off charts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both refer to a singular, recent model output and neither expects ambiguity because there was indeed a recent update; the phrase feels operationally sufficient, especially since the directional findings remain similar.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the package 'final by Thursday' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Ava means ready for leadership review on Thursday morning: storyline locked, main charts inserted, and no major open questions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means approved for same-day external sharing on Thursday afternoon: numbers frozen, memo and appendix reconciled, caveats added, and references polished.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadlines are often discussed in shorthand during coordination meetings, and both see Thursday as the obvious target date; the hidden divergence is in the quality bar, not the date itself.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Marcus will 'update the deck' after receiving Ava's materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Ava assumes this means light edits: replacing charts, tightening wording, and adding one partner-friendly slide while preserving the current structure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus assumes this includes expanding the deck to cover policy guardrails, redemption stress assumptions, and a fuller CBDC comparison section for partner discussions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional business settings, 'update the deck' is a routine phrase that usually goes unelaborated; both parties infer the natural extension from their own downstream audience and see no reason to spell it out.
